purpose: Adds a CodebaseIndex system that syntactically extracts symbols, import edges, and caller/callee call-graph edges from the full checkout and injects a bounded per-file '## Codebase Context (Cross-File Analysis)' section into review prompts so the reviewer can detect cross-file bugs (broken imports, missing exports, renamed-but-unupdated callers).
riskRationale: The feature is enabled by default and runs a synchronous full-repo scan on the review hot path, which can block the event loop for seconds on large monorepos; the headline broken-import detection also misclassifies query-string/fragment asset imports (./icon.svg?url) as broken local imports. Failures degrade gracefully to a diff-only review, the cache is stored outside the checkout (OS temp dir) with atomic writes and per-entry structural validation, and 23+ tests cover the main paths. Remaining issues are fixable accuracy/perf defects in a heuristic feature, not correctness or security flaws.
breakingChanges: Review prompts now include a '## Codebase Context (Cross-File Analysis)' section by default for every PR; disable with review.enableCodebaseIndex: false.
The action bundle grows from ~2.9MB to ~7.6MB (typescript promoted to a runtime dependency for the compiler API).
The codebase index is now built by default (enableCodebaseIndex=true), adding cold-start latency to the first review of each ref.

text: This is a well-engineered feature: ref-SHA-keyed caching with atomic temp-file+rename writes and per-entry structural validation lives outside the checkout in the OS temp dir, per-file relevance filtering with format caps keeps injected context bounded, and the whole indexing path degrades gracefully to a diff-only review. The main concerns are the synchronous, event-loop-blocking full-repo walk on the default-on review hot path and a confirmed false positive in the broken-import detector for query-string asset imports; several extraction-accuracy edge cases (phantom CJS exports, dropped CJS exports in TS files, phantom default-import callee names, unindexed anonymous default exports, intra-file calls labeled as external callers, unbounded cache growth, unused WorkspaceInfo) also deserve attention before merge.

reasoning: Two important issues remain before this is safe on the default path: a synchronous full-repo walk blocks the event loop during the default-enabled index build, and query-string/fragment asset imports are reported as broken local imports, which can trigger spurious findings. Both are fixable — the query-string one is a small self-contained change, the blocking one needs an async/worker refactor — and the remaining minor issues are syntactic-extraction accuracy gaps worth tightening to avoid false cross-file signals in reviews.

message: The cache was moved outside the git checkout (OS temp dir namespaced by a SHA-256 of the repo root) with atomic temp-file+rename writes and per-entry structural validation on read. This closes the trust-boundary concern where attacker-controlled PR content committed to the tree could be loaded as a trusted index, and avoids committing multi-MB JSON into CI checkouts.

Graceful degradation is thorough: the whole indexing path is wrapped in try/catch with a core.warning, formatCodebaseContext guards index/data availability and catches formatting errors, and a build-time >5s warning is surfaced without failing the review. This matches the project's error-resilience conventions.

getContextForFiles relevance-filters the full index down to only what touches changed files, and formatContext applies per-section caps (100 symbols, 150 edges) with truncation notices and drops a section entirely when nothing is relevant, keeping the injected prompt context bounded on large repositories.

isValidIndex validates not just array-ness but per-entry field types (symbols/imports/callGraph), so a schema-drifted or hand-edited cache file degrades to a rebuild instead of rendering undefined garbage into the review prompt. Good defense in depth.

The 10K-file performance sanity check exercises the hot resolveLocalImport path with ~20 filesystem probes per specifier and asserts an explicit time bound, giving the <5s acceptance criterion teeth. The 23 test cases in codebase-index.test.ts (masking, dedupe, cache corruption, performance) are real behavior tests, not mocks, and the monorepo engine test verifies that repo-root-relative ChangedFile.path values match index entries when workDir is a package subdirectory.

buildOrLoad() runs the entire index build synchronously on the review hot path: extractor.extract() uses only blocking APIs (fs.readFileSync/readdirSync/statSync/existsSync) and engine adds cp.execFileSync('git status --porcelain') per review. For the long-running Probot App, a full-repo walk + parse blocks the event loop for the entire build (~0.5s at 10K files, far longer on 100K-file monorepos), stalling concurrent reviews and webhook handling. The async buildOrLoad() signature is also misleading — it returns an already-resolved promise.
suggestion: Move extraction off the main thread (worker thread or child process) or convert to async fs/promises with a bounded concurrency pool; at minimum run the git status/rev-parse probes and the file walk asynchronously (e.g. await setImmediate() every N files) so the event loop can breathe between I/O. Keep the per-ref cache so only the first review of a ref pays the cost.

message: isExternalSpecifier() tests the raw specifier with a $-anchored asset-extension regex, so query-string/fragment asset imports commonly used in Vite/Next projects (./icon.svg?url, ./data.json?raw, ./styles.module.css?inline) fail the asset check, then resolveLocalImport() returns '' and formatContext() reports them as 'Unresolved Local Imports (possible broken imports)'. This produces false-positive findings in the headline broken-import detection (verified empirically: only ./icon.svg?url and ./data.json?raw were flagged, while the real missing-import heuristic is meant to catch genuinely broken relative imports).
suggestion: Strip the query string and fragment before classification so asset imports keep being treated as external and never reach the broken-import list.

message: The CJS export regex /(?:module\.)?exports(?:\.(\w+))?\s*=/ is unanchored, so any substring 'exports' matches: obj.exports = 2 on a plain object yields a phantom exported symbol named 'default', and fooexports.bar = 3 yields a phantom exported 'bar' (verified empirically). These phantom 'exported' symbols pollute the index and can mislead the reviewer about what a changed file actually exports.
suggestion: Require a non-word/non-dot boundary before 'exports' so only real module-level exports match, e.g. add a negative lookbehind: /(?<![.\w])(?:module\.)?exports(?:\.(\w+))?\s*=/g (keep the lookbehind only after confirming the project's minimum Node version supports it).

message: Regex-extracted module.exports/exports.x symbols are only pushed for JS-family files (if (isJs || !sourceFile)), so .ts/.mts/.cts files using CommonJS exports record zero exported symbols. Verified: 'const { helper } = require("./helper.js"); module.exports = { helper };' in a .ts file yields an empty symbol list. The comment claims TS exports are already handled by the AST pass, which is false for CJS-style exports — the AST only sees 'export' keywords. This is a blind spot for the feature's stated missing-export detection in mixed CJS/ESM TypeScript codebases.
suggestion: Push regex symbols for TS-family files too — there is no name-collision risk since AST identifiers cannot be named 'default' — or at minimum for .cts/.mts where CJS is idiomatic.

message: Default-import call edges record phantom callee names: sourceSymbolName is only set for named-import elements, so resolveCallTarget falls back to the local binding alias (name: edge.sourceSymbolName ?? name). Verified: 'import build from "./x.js"; build()' where x.ts's default export is named 'main' produces the edge {calleeFile: "src/x.ts", calleeFunction: "build"} — no such symbol exists in x.ts. The rendered 'Callers of Changed Files' context can therefore report calls to symbols that don't exist in the target module, undermining the renamed-but-unupdated-callers detection with false signals.
suggestion: For default-import edges, resolve the target file's actual default-export symbol name from the index before emitting the edge, or emit calleeFunction as '<default>' when it cannot be resolved, so caller edges reference a name that actually exists in the callee module.

message: Anonymous default exports (export default function () {} and export default class {}) produce no IndexedSymbol at all: extractSymbols skips unnamed function/class declarations, and the defaultExportNames pass only handles identifier expressions. A changed file whose default export is anonymous (very common in React components) contributes nothing to 'Exported Symbols in Changed Files', so the index cannot flag a removed/renamed default export for those files — a gap in the PR's stated 'missing exports' detection goal.
suggestion: When an ExportAssignment expression is a function/class expression without a name, synthesize a symbol named e.g. 'default' with kind 'function'/'class', isDefaultExport: true, isExported: true, so the default export is always represented in the index.

message: getContextForFiles pushes every edge whose calleeFile is a changed file into affectedCallers, including edges where the caller is the SAME changed file (intra-file local calls, callerFile === calleeFile). formatContext renders these under 'Callers of Changed Files', which the type doc (types.ts:101) describes as external callers, so self-contained internal calls look like cross-file callers in the prompt and overstate the blast radius of a change.
suggestion: Exclude intra-file edges from affectedCallers (e.g. if (edge.callerFile !== edge.calleeFile && isChanged(edge.calleeFile))), so the cross-file view only surfaces genuine external callers of changed symbols.

message: CodebaseIndexCache entries are never evicted: one multi-MB JSON per ref SHA accumulates under os.tmpdir()/opencode-codebase-index/<repoHash>/ with no size cap or TTL. On the long-running App (many repos x many PR refs) this grows without bound, and the cached index JSON for a 10K-file repo is several MB each.
suggestion: Add eviction to CodebaseIndexCache — e.g. cap entries per repo (keep the N most recent by mtime) or a TTL sweep on get(), and expose a size guard before writing.

message: WorkspaceInfo (detectWorkspace/readWorkspaceGlobs/readWorkspaceName) is computed and stored on every index but nothing consumes it: grep confirms no caller reads index.workspace, and engine/prompt/formatContext never use it. This is inert monorepo 'awareness' that adds per-extract filesystem reads and index payload weight without behavior, contradicting the PR description's monorepo-awareness claim.
suggestion: Either consume WorkspaceInfo (e.g. resolve imports across workspace packages or scope the relevance filter by workspace globs) or defer the detection to the follow-up language-strategy work and drop it for now to avoid dead data.
